# The Feedback Loom

Every durable system joins observation to action. A map is useful only when each path can be checked against its source.

## Observation

Observation turns events into evidence. Evidence remains useful when it preserves context, location, and sequence.

Feedback begins when an observation changes the next action. Without a source anchor, feedback becomes speculation.

## Action

Action applies evidence to a decision. The decision can be revised when later observation reveals a different pattern.

Therefore observation and action form a feedback loop. The loop remains trustworthy because every claim returns to its source.

## Reflection

Reflection compares earlier evidence with later outcomes. It connects observation, action, and feedback across time.

However reflection is not invention. It must retain the source anchors that let a reader inspect the original passage.
